newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Two Singapore traders buy 1.35 mln bbls of diesel.
newsitem.headline: Two Singapore traders buy 1.35 mln bbls of diesel.

text.p: Two Singapore oil trading companies bought on Tuesday at least 1.35 million barrels of 0.5-percent sulphur diesel in nine cargoes for end-April/early May lifting, traders said.

Traders said Sanko Oil Pte Ltd bought two 150,000-barrel cargoes from French oil company Total at $26.40 per barrel for May 4-8 lifting free-on-board (fob) basis and another cargo at $26.80 for April 23-27 lifting.
Sanko also bought the same volume for the same dates from European major British Petroleum at similar price levels.

Sanko's sister company Hin Leong Trading bought five cargoes--two cargoes from European major Shell at $26.20 and $26.40 for early May lifting fob, one from Swiss trader Glencore at $26.50 for early May, one from US major Mobil at $27 for end-April lifting, and one from western trader Cargill at $26.60 for April 29-May 3 lifting.
With these huge one-day purchases, the two Singapore traders have bought almost 10 million barrels of diesel since they started their buying frenzy on March 3.
This has helped support regional diesel despite the arrival of about 1.6 million tonnes of arbitrage cargoes from the West and boosted Asian refining margins to their best level in over a year.
